title: Job authority and high-access scope
audience: Trainees, new workers and supervisors on the window cleaning (all heights) track who decide whether a window or facade job can start. Completing this lesson does not grant any authority to work at height.
learningOutcomes: Identify who holds site authority, who controls access, and which approvals must exist before any height work is considered.
Separate verified site facts from assumptions and unknowns when scoping a high-access window job.
Apply a stop-work or referral decision to a simulated job pack where authority or competence is missing.

instruction.heading: Why authority comes first
instruction.body: A window job that looks simple from the ground can carry the same fall and falling-object risks as a construction task. Before any height is considered, someone with control of the building or site must confirm in writing what work is wanted, where it will happen, who will be exposed, and who is responsible for the risk. A request from a tenant, a strata committee member or a family member does not by itself establish that the owner or site controller has approved access, equipment or a work area. The first question is therefore not how to reach the windows but who has authority to let the work happen, and on what terms. Under the national working-heights page, high risk construction work is construction carrying a fall risk greater than 2 metres (no date shown).

instruction.heading: Scope the work before planning access
instruction.body: Write the scope in plain terms: the windows or facade panels included, the levels, the surfaces, any frames or fixtures excluded, the cleaning method, and the hours when work may take place. Mark every part of the scope you cannot see from ground level. Glazing condition, frame condition and the structure that carries any platform or anchor are unknowns until a competent person has checked them. This course does not teach glazing repair, sealant or frame work, or structural inspection of facades. If a customer asks for any of those, record the request and refer it rather than agreeing to it.

instruction.heading: Apply the height hierarchy
instruction.body: Safe Work Australia's working-heights page sets the control order: work on the ground where possible, then fall prevention devices, then work-positioning systems, with fall arrest last (no date shown). The SafeWork NSW construction page gives the same order and requires a safe work method statement where a fall could exceed 2 metres (no date shown). Ask whether the windows can be reached from the ground by a water-fed pole or another ground-based method, and only then consider access equipment. South Australia sets the high-risk threshold at 2 metres from 1 July 2026 (page dated 5 June 2026). The ACT sets the same 2-metre SWMS trigger (no date shown), and the Northern Territory construction code gives falls of more than 2 metres as an example (code last varied 12 January 2026). The Victorian, Queensland, Western Australian and Tasmanian pages checked give no metre figure, so check the rule for your state before starting.

instruction.heading: Recognise stop-work conditions
instruction.body: Stop, make the area safe, and report before continuing if any of these apply: there is no written authority from the site controller; the access equipment or anchor has not been inspected; the public or neighbouring property cannot be kept clear of falling objects; the wind or weather is outside the job plan; or the glass or frame looks cracked, loose or unstable. A customer who wants the job finished today is not a reason to work past any of these conditions. The work is also a stop if it falls outside your training or the job pack.

instruction.heading: Record facts, assumptions and approvals separately
instruction.body: Your job record should keep three kinds of entry apart: what you verified by direct observation, what you were told but could not check, and what remains unknown. For each approval the job needs, record the person who gave it, the date, and the scope they approved. The record must also name who decides on a referral and who must be told of a stop-work decision. Do not write that a job is safe or compliant. Write what was checked, what was not, and what must happen next.

instruction.heading: Licence and authority boundary
instruction.body: Licence notice: This lesson does not grant a licence, certificate or authority to work at height or to operate any platform. In New South Wales and Queensland, a boom-type platform needs a WP licence at a boom length of 11 metres or more, and a shorter boom may not need it in those states. The Victorian WP class page (reviewed 30 June 2026) gives the class with no boom-length threshold. Check your state or territory rules and obtain written authorisation from your employer before any work above ground level.

procedure: Confirm the identity and authority of the person who controls the building or site, and record their name and role.
Write the scope: included windows or panels, levels, surfaces, exclusions, method and working hours.
List every part of the scope you cannot verify from ground level and mark each one as an unknown.
Apply the height hierarchy and record whether a ground-based method can meet the scope.
If a fall could exceed two metres, or access equipment is needed, record that a written safe work method statement and competent oversight are required, and check the state rule.
Check the stop-work conditions and record any that apply.
Issue a hold notice if authority, access or competence is missing, and name the person who must resolve it.
Record the decision, the people told and the approvals still outstanding before the job is rescheduled.

workedExamples.situation: A building manager asks for the upper-level windows of a four-storey office to be cleaned next Tuesday. No contractor risk assessment has been provided, and nobody has confirmed whether the building has fixed anchors or a permanent access system.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: What is the first safe action, and who must be told?
workedExamples.reasoning: Treat this as a hold, not a booking. Tell the building manager in writing that the job cannot be scheduled until authority, the access method and the risk assessment are confirmed. Ask for the building's access arrangements and any anchor records. Record the request, the date, the names involved and the unknowns. Do not attend the roof or agree a time until the site controller approves a plan.

workedExamples.situation: A homeowner wants the second-storey windows of a house cleaned and says a ladder will do. The windows are above a paved area where children play, and the ladder reach is uncertain.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: Which method should be considered first, and what must be recorded?
workedExamples.reasoning: Consider a ground-based method first, such as a water-fed pole where the equipment and site allow it, after checking for overhead power lines. In New South Wales, the 2026 SafeWork NSW code sets 3.0 m for ordinary persons near lines up to 132,000 V, and 4.0 m for conductive materials near low-voltage overhead service lines; a water-fed pole is conductive, so the 4.0 m figure applies to it near low-voltage lines. A ladder for height work needs the same authority gate and a safety check.

equipmentAndPpe: Job pack with written scope, site controller contact and approval record
Site plan or photographs marked with levels and exclusion zones
Hold notice template and job record with verified and unknown columns
Eye protection and footwear suited to the task, as specified in the job pack

commonErrors.error: Treating a tenant's or occupant's request as the site controller's approval.
commonErrors.prevention: Confirm the person with control of the building or site and record their approval in writing.

commonErrors.error: Writing the job as safe or compliant in the record.
commonErrors.prevention: Never issue a safety or compliance statement.

commonErrors.error: Assuming a ladder or platform is suitable without checking the anchor, ground or weather.
commonErrors.prevention: Apply the height hierarchy and stop if the equipment, anchor or conditions are unverified.

commonErrors.error: Scheduling the job before the risk assessment is received.
commonErrors.prevention: Issue a hold notice and reschedule only after the approvals are recorded.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Work-at-height hierarchy: the national working-heights page says to work on the ground where possible, then use fall prevention, work positioning and fall arrest last (no date shown). The SafeWork NSW construction page gives the same order (no date shown).

Where a fall could exceed 2 metres, the NSW construction page requires a safe work method statement (no date shown). South Australia uses the same 2-metre threshold from 1 July 2026, the ACT uses it for SWMS, and the Northern Territory code gives it as an example. The other pages checked give no metre figure.

Licence and height notice: This lesson does not grant the right to work at height, on roofs, from elevated work platforms, or on solar systems, and completing it is not a licence, certificate or authority for regulated work. In New South Wales and Queensland, a boom-type elevating work platform needs a WP high risk work licence where its boom is 11 metres or more, so a shorter boom may not need it in those states. The NSW page, the Tasmanian page (last updated 1 December 2023), the Western Australian page (published 11 August 2026, updated 13 August 2026) and the Northern Territory bulletin (no date shown) each state that threshold. The Queensland page places platforms shorter than 11 metres outside its definition (no date shown). The Victorian WP page gives the class with no boom-length threshold (reviewed 30 June 2026), so the licence is not limited by length there. Check whether this work needs a high-risk work licence with the state regulator before you start. The national model code uses the same 11-metre threshold, measured from the original design, and requires no licence for shorter booms, although the operator must still be trained (model code, December 2025). Scissor lifts need no WP licence in Victoria (reviewed 30 June 2026) or the Northern Territory (no date shown); the other pages checked do not address them. Check your state or territory rule and obtain written employer authorisation before any work above ground level.
The Safe Work Australia model code on managing the risk of falls at workplaces is a model. Its legal effect depends on each jurisdiction, and its publication date is blank (no date shown).

qualityStandard: Written authority from the site controller is on file before any height work is considered.
The scope lists included and excluded windows, levels and methods.
Every unknown is marked, and no unverified item is described as safe.
A stop-work or referral decision is recorded for every missing approval.
documentationEvidence: Name, role and approval date of the person with site authority
Written scope with included and excluded items
Verified facts, unverified statements and unknowns, recorded separately
Hold, stop-work or referral record with the person notified and the approval still outstanding
summary: Authority to work at height comes from the site controller in writing, not from a request alone.
Apply the height hierarchy before choosing any access method.
Stop and refer when authority, access, anchor, weather or competence is unverified.
This lesson grants no licence or authority, and state rules must be checked for each job.

knowledgeChecks.question: A tenant asks for the upper windows of a managed building to be cleaned this week. What must be confirmed before a height plan is considered?
options: That the tenant has paid for the service in advance and the rent
That the window cleaner has a ladder in the van and a rope
That the weather forecast is clear for the whole week ahead
Written approval from the person with control of the building or site

knowledgeChecks.question: Which step comes first in the height hierarchy for a window job?
options: Eliminate the need to work at height
Use fall-arrest systems on the roof
Use work-positioning systems on the frame
Use scaffolding without a plan

knowledgeChecks.question: Under the NSW construction guidance, what document is required where a fall could exceed two metres?
options: A glazing certificate for it
A safe work method statement
A tenancy agreement for the unit
A council parking permit

knowledgeChecks.question: Which entry correctly records an unverified glazing condition?
options: Glazing is safe to clean as it is and sound overall
Glazing is compliant with the building code on the site
Glazing condition is unknown until a competent person checks it
Glazing needs no check before the work starts on the site

knowledgeChecks.question: Does completing this lesson grant authority to work at height?
options: Yes, for ground-floor windows and the entry and the sill
Yes, once the quiz is passed by the worker and the site
Yes, if the employer agrees to it in writing today
No, the lesson grants no licence, certificate or authority
